summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — RKT.L +5%, AI.PA +3%, BP.L +3%, TTE.PA +3%, BNZL.L +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (RHM.DE -6%, ENR.DE -5%, ADYEN.AS -5%, EDV.L -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: RHM.DE (-5.54%) — No single-day headline — fell amid ongoing 2026 defense-sector de-rating/profit-taking, despite a same-day Deutsche Bank buy reiteration (PT €1,800) and LUNA NG drone type-approval news. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — RHM.DE is a German XETRA large-cap defense/industrials name, a sector not covered by uk-eu equity universes, so no filter ever saw the drop to react to.

top_movers.catalyst: Mead Johnson (Reckitt unit) won first federal Enfamil baby-formula NEC lawsuit; JPMorgan also upgraded RKT to 'overweight' same day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RKT.L is a large-cap UK consumer-staples name (FTSE 100), a sector/cap bucket the bot's momentum/news strategies don't currently cover.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a FTSE 100 consumer-staples sleeve with an event-driven overlay that flags litigation-outcome/RNS headlines and analyst rating changes, not just earnings surprises.

top_movers.catalyst: Elliott disclosed an activist stake pushing for margin improvements vs. Linde, plus Mizuho initiated at Outperform (€200 PT) — stock +3.3% while CAC 40 fell.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AI.PA is a large-cap French industrial gas name, likely excluded because uk-eu strategies are scoped to a narrower sector/index list that doesn't cover industrials on Euronext Paris.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-driven activist/13D-style watch layer that flags large-cap EU names on stake-disclosure headlines, so the universe temporarily includes them for next-day evaluation even if outside the core sector list.

top_movers.catalyst: Brent crude spiked above $90/bbl after US and Iran exchanged strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, lifting oil majors like BP.L on supply-disruption fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BP.L (UK-listed integrated oil major) is likely excluded via a sector/commodity carve-out; the move was a macro geopolitical oil-price spike, not a stock-specific signal, so no filter ever evaluated it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a commodity-linked equity bucket (major integrated oils incl. BP.L, Shell) to the uk-eu universe, gated on a Brent %-move trigger (e.g. >=3% in a session) so geopolitical oil spikes route to a macro-news strategy.

top_movers.catalyst: Brent crude jumped >2% (~$90-92/bbl) on renewed US-Iran clashes near Strait of Hormuz, lifting European oil majors incl. TTE, Orlen, OMV in sympathy.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — TTE.PA is a large-cap European energy name, so no momentum/mean-reversion strategy tracks it; the move was a sector-wide beta reaction to a geopolitical oil shock, not a stock-specific signal any in-universe filter would have flagged.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small EU energy-majors basket (TTE.PA, SHEL, BP, OMV) to the universe gated on a Brent-crude ≥1.5% intraday move, so geopolitical oil shocks get captured via a sector proxy rather than requiring name-by-name coverage.

top_movers.catalyst: H1 2026 results beat (rev +2.9% cc, adj. EPS +11% YoY), raised FY guidance, and new £500m buyback amid Elliott activist pressure for more capital return.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Bunzl is a FTSE 100 UK business-services/distribution large-cap, a sector/geography bucket the bot's uk-eu strategies don't currently scan, so no technical filter ever saw the earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 industrials/distribution constituents to the uk-eu universe, or add a sector-agnostic earnings-day gap scanner flagging FTSE 100 names with post-results moves ≥2% at open.

top_movers.catalyst: No single Sep-1 headline; move extends a rebound (+8.6% in 7 sessions) off the M&S pan-European fulfilment-partnership news and an oversold bounce from the Aug 4 guidance cut.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Zalando is a ~€6.5B German SDAX/MDAX online-fashion retailer, a mid-cap EU consumer-discretionary name likely excluded by market-cap/sector scope rather than any technical filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Widen uk-eu universe inclusion to MDAX/SDAX consumer-discretionary names above a €5B cap floor, or add an explicit e-commerce/retail sector bucket, so multi-day recovery rallies like this become visible to momentum strategies.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RHM.DE is a German XETRA large-cap defense/industrials name, a sector not covered by uk-eu equity universes, so no filter ever saw the drop to react to.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a defense/industrials sector bucket (XETRA large-caps incl. RHM.DE) to the uk-eu universe with a crowded-trade-unwind filter (e.g. flag ≥5% single-day drop after >20% 6-month run-up).

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh firm-specific news; extension of sector-wide wind/power-equipment de-rating (GE Vernova's weak wind margins) and profit-taking that followed ENR's Aug 31 record Q3 orders/earnings beat.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ENR.DE is a XETRA-listed, ~€120B German industrial/power-equipment large-cap; bot's universe is likely US-equity/ADR-focused and doesn't cover EU exchange-listed names, so no filter ever saw it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU large-cap XETRA/Frankfurt listings (mkt cap >€50B) to the tradable universe, tagged by sector, so cross-name contagion moves in the wind/power-equipment complex (ENR.DE, GE Vernova, Nordex) become visible to momentum filters.

top_movers.catalyst: No single clear news trigger found for 09-01; move looks like continuation of Adyen's 2026 downtrend (stock ~34% YTD lower on EU payments-competition worries), landing the same day a new EMEA president (Nicole Olbe) took over — likely technical/sector drift, not a fresh headline.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — ADYEN.AS is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam fintech/payments name; a 'uk-eu' universe likely scopes to UK indices plus select EU blue-chips or excludes names with extreme trailing volatility/drawdown, and Adyen's multi-quarter -70%-from-highs profile probably trips a max
top_movers.suggestion: Add an EU large-cap (e.g. AEX/Euronext top-40) bucket to the uk-eu universe, or if excluded by a volatility/drawdown filter, add a carve-out that re-admits mega-cap (>€20B) names regardless of trailing drawdown so structurally-battered blue chips aren't permanently locked out.

top_movers.catalyst: Gold pulled back near $4,450/oz after Fed's Warsh signaled more tightening may be needed, dragging LSE gold miners incl. Endeavour Mining lower sector-wide.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EDV.L is a UK-listed pure-play gold miner (materials/commodity sector), a category the bot's equity strategies likely exclude given no direct commodity-price signal input.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gold-miner basket (e.g. EDV.L, FRES.L) gated on a spot-gold/DXY proxy signal so sector-wide moves driven by rate expectations are catchable without new single-name coverage.
